博物彙編 草木典 第二百三十四卷 柿部 (Bowu huibian, Caomu dian, juan 234, persimmon section)

facsimile/page0105.jpg is the section table of contents, which lists
"王象晉群芳譜{蕃柿}" among the sources excerpted.
Retrieved 2026-08-30.

THE PASSAGE, verified character by character against the facsimile:

王象晉羣芳譜
蕃柿
蕃柿一名六月柿，莖似蒿，高四五尺，葉似艾，花似榴。一枝結五實，
或三四實，一樹二三十實，縛作架，最堪觀。火傘、火珠，未足為喻。
草本也，來自西番，故名。

"Fanshi, also called liuyueshi (sixth-month persimmon). Stem like wormwood,
four or five feet high; leaves like mugwort; flowers like pomegranate. One
branch bears five fruits, or three or four; one plant twenty or thirty fruits.
TIED UP TO MAKE A FRAME, IT IS MOST WORTH LOOKING AT. 'Fire-parasol' and
'fire-pearl' are not adequate comparisons. It is a herbaceous plant. It came
from the Western barbarians, hence the name."

WHY THIS MATTERS: 縛作架，最堪觀 ("tied up to make a frame, it is most worth
looking at") is the ornamental-cultivation statement. Until now that claim rested
on the 1728 Pianzi Leibian quotation alone. This is a SECOND, INDEPENDENT imperial
compilation quoting the same 1621 original, and it is FACSIMILE-VERIFIED.
